newsitem.title: PERU: Three Peru hostages at serious health risk - paper.
newsitem.headline: Three Peru hostages at serious health risk - paper.

text.p: Three of the 103 remaining hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima are suffering serious health problems and should be evacuated, a former captive who is a doctor told a Peruvian newspaper on Friday.

Victor Lucero Rondon told El Comercio Dominican Republic Ambassador Victor Lucero Rondon was suffering from diabetes "that can at any time (cause) a brain problem," Peruvian Supreme Court President Moises Pantoja's heart condition made him a "high-risk case," and Energy and Mines Vice Minister Juan Mendoza had a hernia "that could potentially get complicated."

The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels have released about 400 captives including all women and elderly since storming the residence on Dec. 17. The remaining captives include two Peruvian ministers, Japanese businessmen, a handful of foreign diplomats and the brother of President Alberto Fujimori.
Lucero said he had treated one of the MRTA rebels who suffered a gunshot wound in the leg during the initial battle.
